claims.conditions: The same project, on the same machine or a machine sharing the gstack state root, where a save has been made in an earlier session or before compaction, so that a checkpoint exists. With no checkpoint the 'to' skill still runs, by a different route, and this relation does not apply.
claims.rationale: The 'to' skill loads checkpoint files from the project's checkpoint directory under the gstack state root; the 'from' skill is what writes them there and says its purpose is that a later session 'can resume without losing a beat via /context-restore' (from line 105). The 'to' skill's verify-first sorting relies on the commit and project identity that the 'from' skill stamps into the checkpoint (from lines 298-308; to lines 280-283, 318-326), and it states reduced ability for checkpoints lacking them (to line 326). Without a prior save the 'to' skill has no checkpoint to load; it then tells the user nothing was saved and rebuilds context by a separate route defined in a section file that was not read (to lines 142, 401-403). This is a mechanical dependency read from the two texts; how much of a session's working state survives a save-then-restore round trip has not been observed. Falsified if a restore with no prior save presents the same remaining-work list as one that follows a save.
